dialogue_texts: The sun has breached the horizon. The parallel layer has receded, and your window of opportunity for the night has closed.
How utterly tedious. To spend an entire evening weaving through gaps and manipulating boundaries, only to be forced back by the sunrise with absolutely nothing to show for it but a nagging headache.
You commanded the boundaries with immense precision, Yukari. But the glohm within that distortion didn't just resist your gaps - it twisted the very concept of distance.
Without a decisive strike to the core, we were merely rearranging the shadows.
Having my own gaps rejected and turned against me by the Order is a novelty I could have easily done without. Failing to restore the balance before dawn is... a rather unsightly blemish on my record.
It is more than an aesthetic issue. Look closely at the hem of your dress. The glohm didn't fade with the dawn. It has anchored itself to your spirit font.
Oh... how deeply unpleasant. It feels incredibly heavy. The boundaries of my own consciousness feel warped, as if the gap between waking and dreaming is blurring.
The glohm is taking root because the core remains completely intact. What is your next move? It will only continue to warp your power if left unchecked.
My fragile little mind has quite tolerated enough of this absurd parallel logic for one morning.
Too bad! Bad ending! To see the good ending, clear the game without using a continue or letting nine hours pass.
